Q: How to fix Pydantic wheel build? A:

Your error log contains this:


  error: the configured Python interpreter version (3.14) is newer than PyO3's maximum supported version (3.13)
        = help: please check if an updated version of PyO3 is available. Current version: 0.22.2
        = help: set PYO3_USE_ABI3_FORWARD_COMPATIBILITY=1 to suppress this check and build anyway using the stable ABI

I'd say that's enough information for you to proceed. PyO3 sits at 0.29.0 now. Otherwise, just set the env var as described in the error message will provably work without changing any other thing there.

Q: Boolean return vs throwing exceptions in C# A:

Exceptions are useful when:

  1. The fault is external and can not reasonably be anticipated by the programmer. A typical example might be an network fault, it could happen at any time and is outside the programmers control. These kinds of failures need to be handled at some higher level.
  2. Incorrect API usage. If you specify that a parameter cannot be null, throwing a null reference exception on null is reasonable. This alerts the programmer to the fault so it can be fixed.

The TryGet-pattern, or equivalent Option/Maybe/Result/nullable patterns, are great when the operation may or may not succeed. A typical example is parsing user inputs. Invalid inputs are expected and needs to be handled.

In your example it will depend on how your class is intended to be used, and what you consider to be "failure". If routes are configured completely statically by the programmer, exceptions might be a valid approach, since that will alert the programmer to an incorrect configuration. If routes are created dynamically I would argue in favor of TryGet, since missing routes will happen and needs to be handled by the caller.

Note that you have a documentation bug. ValidateReplacement can throw, and is called from AddRoute, but AddRoute does not document the exception. If an Add method returns a bool I would assume that it does not throw, and this assumption is reinforced by the current documentation of AddRoute. GetRoute has no documentation, so is even more difficult to use correctly.

I would also recommend reading Eric lipperts article on Vexing Exceptions for some more details on the types of exceptions and how to use them.

Q: Amplify deployments are failing due to error saying Unable to assume specified IAM Role (Backend app) A:

If you're deploying your app using a GitHub webhook connection, the "Unable to assume role" error can sometimes be misleading. This may occur if AWS Amplify no longer has the required read/write access to your GitHub repository.

To verify the repository permissions:

  1. Log in to your GitHub account (personal or organization).

  2. Go to Settings → GitHub Apps → AWS Amplify → Configure.

  3. Scroll down to the Repository Access section.

  4. Ensure All repositories is selected, or explicitly grant access to the repository connected to your Amplify app.

After updating the permissions, trigger a new deployment. If Amplify had lost access to the repository, the deployment should proceed without the "Unable to assume role" error.
